newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian Unibanka signs CSFB for planned eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Latvian Unibanka signs CSFB for planned eurobond.

text.p: Latvia's Unibanka said on Tuesday that it has chosen Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) to lead a planned eurobond issue.
The bank, Latvia's second largest, has said that it plans a small eurobond in the summer but has not given an amount.

"Unibanka yesterday signed a mandate with leading investment bank Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB), which will undertake the coordination and placing of Unibanka's eurobond issue," the bank said in a statement.
Unibanka said that it has already cooperated with CSFB, which has offered the Latvian bank foreign exchange lines and international trade finance lines.
"This operation will allow Unibanka to get new, cheaper long-term resources from the Western market," the bank added.
A spokeswoman for the bank said the size of the eurobond had still not been decided.
Unibanka is part state-owned, although the government has said it wants to sell most of its remaining 33 percent.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and Swedfund are also major shareholders.
It made a first quarter profit of 1.4 million lats.
The bank said the eurobond would also allow it to lower its interest rates and to offer more long-term loans.
The bank is also expected soon to launch a global depository receipt (GDR) issue, planned at around $10 million.
